Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of painful, cracked, itchy palmar skin likely secondary to irritant contact dermatitis from occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals without glove protection.  
- DDx from reasoning system supports irritant contact dermatitis (high likelihood) and allergic contact dermatitis (moderate likelihood). No features suggesting systemic disease; no evidence for infection or psoriasis.  
- Plan discussed:  
  • Avoidance of triggers; wear protective gloves consistently at work.  
  • Prescription of topical steroid cream (potency not documented) to reduce inflammation.  
  • Prescription of stronger emollient; apply liberally 3–4 times daily for 10–14 days.  
  • Safety-net: return sooner if spreading or worsening; routine review in 1–2 weeks if not resolved.  
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx noted.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Irritant contact dermatitis of the hands – High likelihood: temporal relationship to new housekeeping job, direct chemical exposure without gloves, painful fissuring > itch.  
2. Allergic contact dermatitis to cleaning products – Moderate likelihood: occupational allergens present; intermittent itch; possible sensitization period.
